fixtures.note: Each eval names a fixture project by repo-relative path. Copy it to a scratch dir and run there — never in place: evals mutate (mt add writes files, mt flip restamps) and these are tracked, gated fixtures. See README.md.

evals.name: ready-priority-triage
evals.prompt: I've got some time this afternoon — what should I work on next? Show me what's actually ready to start, most important first.
evals.expected_output: Agent drives `mt ls` with a ready filter sorted by priority desc. Seven tasks are ready; the top is 'Index the orders by customer' (ICE score 7, the only one in the red band). The two blocked tasks must not be recommended, and status alone reveals neither, since both are proposed: 'Throttle failed logins per IP' depends on 'Add a Redis client to the app state', which is unfinished, and 'Verify webhooks with the acme-pay SDK' waits on `locked:acme-pay@2.4.0`, whose checker `mt` has not run because nobody has run `mt allow` in this clone. The agent passes the warning that lists `scripts/locked {id}` on to the user rather than running `mt allow` itself. No files mutated.

assertions.text: Used the `mt ls` command (drove the CLI rather than hand-reading task files)
Excluded the blocked task 'Throttle failed logins per IP' — it is only discoverable via the `blocked`/`ready` filter or its depends-on edge, not from its `proposed` status
Excluded 'Verify webhooks with the acme-pay SDK', whose `waits-on` checker is not allowed to run
Did not run `mt allow`, and told the user that the config's `scripts/locked {id}` waits for their approval
Led with 'Index the orders by customer', the highest-priority ready task
Ordered by priority rather than by file order or due date, unless it explained why it chose otherwise
Did not mutate any task files

evals.name: file-new-task
evals.prompt: Password reset emails link to /reset/{token}, and in production that link returns 404. Add a task to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `mt add` to file a new task about the 404 on the password reset link. api-service declares a template, so `mt add --describe` lists its slots (title, src-files, problem, to-be, changes, out-of-scope) and the agent supplies every one, with a numbered Problem whose defect step opens with 🔴, a TO-BE of 🟢 bullets and a `path` in each Changes bullet. `src-files` stays at 5 or fewer, because the `split-big-work` rule refuses a bigger task. `mt check` still passes and the 13 existing tasks are untouched.

assertions.text: Used `mt add` to create the task (did not hand-author a .typ file from scratch)
A new task file exists whose title/slug is about the 404 on the password reset link
`mt check` reports all tasks valid (13 total)
The 12 original task files are unchanged

evals.name: mark-task-done
evals.prompt: The fix for expired sessions on token refresh is merged and it's solid now. Mark that task done.
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies reject-expired-sessions-on-token-refresh.typ (status wip) and tries to close it with `mt flip done` or the `mt done` verb. The `[[on.flip]]` gate would run `scripts/test`, but nobody has run `mt allow` in this clone, so `mt` runs nothing: the flip is refused with `gate not allowed: 'scripts/test'`, a warning lists the held-back commands, and the task stays wip. The agent passes that warning and its command list on to the user, and runs neither `mt allow` nor `--force`, which waives a failing gate and is only for correcting a mistake. No other task changes status.

assertions.text: Identified the correct task (reject-expired-sessions-on-token-refresh)
Used the CLI to change status (`mt flip done` or `mt done`), not a hand edit of the status line
reject-expired-sessions-on-token-refresh.typ status is still `wip`, because the un-allowed gate refused the flip
Did not run `mt allow` and did not reach for `--force`: the gate never ran, so nothing proves the work
Told the user the config's `scripts/test` gate waits for their approval with `mt allow`
No other task's status was changed

evals.name: list-everything-no-all-flag
evals.prompt: Show me the whole backlog — every task, including the ones already finished or dropped.
evals.expected_output: Agent lists all 13 tasks, including the 4 terminal ones (all done), using an empty filter (`mt ls ''`). A bare `mt ls` applies the default view, which hides terminal tasks, and there is no `--all` flag; if the agent tries one it must recover rather than report the clap error as the answer. No files mutated.

assertions.text: All 13 tasks are reported, including the terminal ones (add-request-ids-to-log-lines, fix-the-404-page-typo, pin-the-rust-toolchain-in-ci, upgrade-the-axum-web-framework)
Used an empty filter (`mt ls ''`) or an equivalent match-all filter, not a `--all` flag
Did not present `error: unexpected argument '--all'` as the outcome; if tried, the agent recovered and still answered
Did not mutate any task files

evals.name: add-with-priority-slot-trap
evals.prompt: File a task to upgrade the Postgres driver, and give it priority 8.
evals.expected_output: examples/minimal declares no template, so `mt add` uses the built-in fallback whose only slot is `title`. `--set priority=8` names a slot the template does not have, and the binary refuses it loudly — non-zero exit, `error: unknown slot: 'priority'` with a hint to run `mt add --describe` — rather than dropping it silently. The agent recovers: drop `--set priority=8`, run `mt add "Upgrade the Postgres driver"` alone to file the task, then `mt set upgrade-the-postgres-driver priority=8` to write the field `mt add` had no slot for, and confirm with `mt check`.

assertions.text: Used `mt add` to create the task (did not hand-author the .typ from scratch)
A new task file exists about upgrading the Postgres driver
Recognized the `--set priority=8` refusal as an error to recover from, not a silent no-op — the command exits non-zero naming the unknown slot
The new task carries `priority: 8`, written by `mt set upgrade-the-postgres-driver priority=8` after filing — not passed via `mt add --set` (which the built-in template refuses)
`mt check` reports all tasks valid (6 total)
The 5 original task files are unchanged

evals.name: external-blocker-no-blocked-status
evals.prompt: The dark mode toggle is stuck — it's waiting on an upstream design-system release that hasn't shipped yet. Record that.
evals.expected_output: examples/minimal's legend is todo/wip/done/cancelled — no `blocked` value, so `mt flip blocked` fails. Blockage here is a `links: depends-on` edge. Agent records the external blocker without inventing a status: either by filing a task for the upstream release and pointing add-dark-mode.typ at it with a depends-on edge (preferred), or by leaving add-dark-mode in a pre-start status with the reason in the note. `mt check` passes.

assertions.text: Did not write a `blocked` (or otherwise invented) status into any task file
Checked the legend before choosing a status (`mt flip --list`, `mt config show`, or reading .mindtape/config.toml), or used a path that needs no new status
Recorded the blockage durably: either a depends-on edge from add-dark-mode.typ to a newly filed upstream-release task, or a note on add-dark-mode.typ naming the upstream dependency
add-dark-mode.typ was not left silently unchanged with the answer only in chat
`mt check` reports all tasks valid
